text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- It is harder for people who are divorced to get state benefits than most other groups, according to an office director at the Social Services Committee who deals with a lot of divorced women seeking allowances.

- Higher inflation than expected means that the base level of pensions will be lifted by an average of 100 crowns to 36,400 crowns next year, according to Statistics Sweden. This means that pensions could increase by between 11 and 38 crowns a month.

- Peter Wallenberg has halved his share holding of forestry group Stora . He sold 200,000 A-series shares worth 25 million crowns, according to a spokesman at Investor, the Wallenberg family's investment vehicle.

- Shares in TV4 fell on Tuesday even though the company reported better results for the first six months of 1997. Its half year profit after financial items was 51.4 million crowns compared to a loss of 34.6 million crowns in the same period last year.

- Finance Minister Erik Asbrink has said no to giving higher benefit levels despite calls from the trade union umbrella group, LO. He told a Social Democratic economic seminar that it may be possible reduce taxes for low and normal income earners when Sweden's budget moves into surplus in 1998 instead of lifting benefit levels.

- Bearings maker SKF posted a half year result of 1.1 billion crowns which was about in line with market expectations. It said the business cycle in Europe was improving but competition in the bearings market was putting pressue on profit margins. Inline skates are turning into a profitable sideline for SKF.

- Higher prices for fresh fruit and vegetables, and for coffee were partly behind a rise in Sweden's consumer price index in June. The CPI rose 0.1 percent against market expectations of a fall of 0.1 percent.
- Only published on Fridays during the summer.
